 Judgment
This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 19.01.2020, the injured petitioner was going towards madanapalle from Horsley Hills as a pillion rider in a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-CF-5794 ridden by his friend Keshava Prasad slowly, cautiously on the left side of the Horsley-Madanapalle road.

On the way at about 3-00 p.m. near Horsley Hills 1 KM mile car bearing Reg.No.AP-27-AN-1119 came from opposite direction at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
In the result, both the occupants of the motorcycle knocked down, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
This accident occurred due to carelessness, rash and negligent driving of the Innova Car by its driver.
Immediately the petitioner was taken to Govt. Hospital, Madanapalle, after first aid he was referred to Sree Ramadevi Multi Speciality Hospital, Tirupathi.

entities.text: Sree Ramadevi Multi Speciality Hospital, Tirupathi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the hospital, injury to right thigh, fracture midshaft of right femur was noticed and treated by open reduction and internal fixation with intramedullay inter locked nailing for fracture shaft of right femur.

The petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 21.01.2020 to 27.01.2020 and again the petitioner got admitted to Tirumala Hospital, Tirupathi on 06.10.2021, in the hospital non union fracture right femur noticed and treated by dynamisation, bone grafting and exchange of distal locking screw and discharged on 07.10.2021.
Thereafter till today the petitioner is under treatment as an outpatient and in spite of treatment, petitioner has not come to normal position physically and functionally.
The Petitioner was a Carpenter and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
After the accident, till today the petitioner is completely bedridden and lost his earnings.
In future the petitioner cannot do his avocation to earn his livelihood due to disability and impediment.
So far the petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards treatment, medicine, conveyance etc. and requires more amount for his future treatment.

As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle,
it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1- Insured and Respondent No.2-insurer.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.

4. The Respondent No.1 has denied all the averments of the petition inter-alia contending that the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, the accident has occurred due to negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Further, as on the date of accident the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2 and same was valid as on the date of accident and the driver was having valid DL.
On these grounds, he has prayed for dismissal of the petition against him.

5. The Respondent No.2 has filed its written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the alleged offending vehicle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in Bheemashankar Reddy K Alias Kanala ... vs Prabhakar S on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177428399/
2 the policy.

entities.text: Bheemashankar Reddy K Alias Kanala ... vs Prabhakar S
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, denied the contents of petition averments in toto.
It has contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

It has denied that the the accident was caused due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and contended that the accident has occurred due to negligence of petitioner, as he was riding the motorcycle without DL.
Further it has contended that the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties as the owner and insurer of motorcycle were not arrayed as respondents in the petition.

It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner,
avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by him, expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.
Further contended that the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant, excessive and unreasonable.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained injuries when he was proceeding as a pillion rider in the Motorcycle bearing No.AP-03-CF-5794 on 19.01.2020 about 3- 00 p.m., near Horsley Hills 1 KM mile stone, B.Kothakota Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, only due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing No.AP-27-AN-1119?
2. What compensation Petitioner is entitled?
3. What order ?
7.

In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case,
one witness is examined as PW-2 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.13.
8.
The Respondents have not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.

9. By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative. Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1:- The case of the petitioner is that on 19.01.2020, the injured petitioner was going towards madanapalle from Horsley Hills as a pillion rider in a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-CF-5794 ridden by his friend Keshava Prasad slowly, cautiously on the left side of the Horsley-Madanapalle road.

On the way at about 3-00 p.m. near Horsley Hills 1 KM mile car bearing Reg.No.AP-27-AN-1119 came from opposite direction at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
In the result, both the occupants of the motorcyle knocked down, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

sentences.text: In order to substantiate his case, petitioner has examined as PW-1 and got marked the police documents at Ex.P.1 to 5 i.e., FIR, complaint, spot sketch, wound certificate and charge sheet.
To support of his claim, Dr.S.A.Somashekara, Orthopedic surgeon is examined as PW-2 and he has produced the documents at Ex.P.12 and 13
The Respondent-insurance company has contended that it was the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle in causing the accident and not on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

During the cross examination of PW1, learned counsel for the respondent no 2 has put forth suggestion that rider motorcycle dashed to the offending vehicle and the accident caused due to his own fault and not fault of the offending vehicle driver.
Same was denied.
Except cross-examination and contention in the objections, respondents have not produced any evidence to prove the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.
13. There are no materials on record to disprove the Petitioner's evidence and to prove the contention of the Respondent.
The evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
After the investigation, police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and the copy of the charge sheet is produced at Ex.P.5.
Charge sheet prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
From all the above documents it is clear that the Petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

14. ISSUE NO.2 :- As per Ex.P.4 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained tenderness over right thigh region - fracture femur and the doctor opined that the above injury is grievous in nature.
15. Due to the accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
Immediately he was taken to Government hospital, Madanapalle and after first aid, he was referred to Sree Ramadevi Multi Speciality hospital, Tirupathi.

entities.text: Sree Ramadevi Multi Speciality hospital, Tirupathi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the hospital after taking X-rays he as diagnosed injury to right thigh and fracture midshaft of right femur and he was treated by open reduction and internal fixation with intramedullary inter locked nailing for fracture shaft of right femur.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was working as a Carpenter and earning a sum of .25,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he has suffered loss of income.
He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.

16. PW-2 Dr.Somashekara, Orthopedic surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, has deposed that the Petitioner has sustained fracture midshaft right femur and he was treated with CRIF with IMIL nailing under SA on 23.01.2020, implant removal and exchange nailing under S.A. on 30.05.2020 and Dynamisation, bone grafting and exchange of distal locking screw on 07.10.2021 was done.
Further, PW-2 has stated that now the petitioner complains of pain and difficulty in walking and climbing stairs.
On examination he has assessed the total disability of right lower limb at 44% and to the whole body physical disability at 22%.

sentences.text: On careful reading of evidence of PW-2 makes it clear the PW-3 has not treated the Petitioner.
During the course of cross examination he denied that the petitioner is not suffering from a disability exceeding 3 % of the whole body .
It is pertinent to note that PW3 has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.

18. The petitioner has stated that he was working as a Carpenter and earning a sum of .25,000/-
p.m.

Considering that the grievous injury is on the leg and considering the difficulties, avocation and evidence of PW-3 and also by considering the age of the Petitioner, the functional disability is assessed at 10%.
19. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 23 years.
Ex. P.10

- Aadhaar card shows that he was born on 19.06.1999, the same is considered as age of the petitioner as on the date of accident as 21 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 18.
20.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work as earlier and has to take help of others to do daily activities.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate his income.
In the absence of material with regard to source of income, the tribunal has to be considered the notional income chart of the Lok Adalath.
21. The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2020, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs 14,500/- Per Month.

Thus, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
22. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability:
Looking into the nature of injuries, it definitely affects the working capacity of any person.
Considering nature of injury and doctor's evidence the total functional disability of the Petitioner is considered at 10%.
Thus, loss of future income comes to Rs.14,500 x 12 x 18 x 10/100= Rs.3,13,200/-.
23. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and was treated as an inpatient which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .30,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
24. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in his day today activities and face hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .25,000/- under loss of amenities of life.
25. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.11 amounting to Rs.6,264/-.
There is no evidence forthcoming to disbelieve the said medical bills.
On perusal of medical bills, it appears that the petitioner has spent Rs.6,264/- towards medical treatment.
The medical bills appears to be genuine.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded compensation of .6,264/- towards Medical Expenses.

Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:

Ex.P.6 -Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was admitted at Government Hospital, Madanapalle, then referred to Sree Ramadevi Multi Speciality Hospital, Tirupathi wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 21.01.2020 to 27.01.2020 and again from 27.05.2020 to 06.06.2020 and again from 13.07.2020 to 27.07.2020 and from 06.10.2021 to 07.10.2021 i.e., totally for a period of 29 days.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Thereafter petitioner got admitted to Sri Balaji Institute of Surgery Research Rehabilitation (BIRRD) hospital, Tirupathi on 27.05.2020 Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .30,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.

entities.text: Balaji Institute of Surgery Research Rehabilitation (BIRRD) hospital, Tirupathi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 27. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to loss of earnings during treatment,
considering 29 days admission in the hospital as inpatient and around 3 months for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 3 months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .14,500/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .14,500/- x 3 = Rs.43,500/-.
28.

Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:
Sl. Nature of Compensation Amount No.
1. Loss of future earnings  3,13,200/-
2. Pain and Sufferings  30,000/-
3. Loss of amenities  25,000/-
4. Medical expenses  6,264/-
5. Conveyance, Food,  30,000/-
 Nourishment & Attendant  charges 6. Loss of income during laid  43,500/-
 up period  Total  4,47,964/-
29.
Liability:
Respondent No.1 being the owner and the Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.
However, Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
30. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
